items.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
items.summary: Complexity theorist and former OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson argues that AI's recent math breakthroughs matter far beyond academia. The possible consequences, he writes, range from reshaping the global economy to threatening all life on Earth. He's also "virtually certain" that AI labs are sitting on "one or more bombshells" in cryptography. items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
items.summary: OpenAI says a billing bug gave GPT-6.2 users incorrect discounts. After the fix, Astra and Sol users hit their limits 40 and 25 percent faster than last week. As an apology, subscribers get an extra reset, and business users get free Fast Mode through year-end. OpenAI is also testing a Chat and Work mode merger. items.title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
items.summary: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites to process AI data as orbital data centers. SpaceX is targeting its first launches in 2027, and the full constellation is set to be operating by 2040. Google and Blue Origin are also working on AI infrastructure in space, but Boston Consulting Group estimates costs will stay well above ground-based data centers for now. items.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
items.summary: Microsoft has published the technical architecture of ARTEX, an AI framework in wide use since July 2026 that runs cyberattacks with specialized agents and almost no human involvement. State-backed groups from China and North Korea, along with criminal organizations, are already using the system. items.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
items.summary: Nvidia has told partners such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. Following new US export controls targeting Chinese cloud access, dealers are already seeking buyers for thousands of B300 chips, while one cloud executive describes "chaos", Loans and major deals are now on the line for Southeast Asia's data centers. items.title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
items.summary: Chip restrictions, anti-distillation measures, and shrinking access to Nvidia hardware abroad are putting growing pressure on Deepseek, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba, according to a report. Deepseek researchers internally estimate they're already up to nine months behind US models, and the gap is widening. items.title: Amazon and Meta are in talks to end the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse in Amazon's online store.
items.summary: Amazon and Meta are in talks to bring back Muse, Meta's AI shopping agent that Amazon kicked off its platform in September. The two sides are stuck on ad revenue and who gets to control search results. That matters because Amazon's ad business generates $68.6 billion a year, and Muse already commands 51 percent of all agentic shopping orders.
